extracted.intended_audience: school administrators, Title IX coordinators, higher education and K-12 institutions, legal counsel, and advocates involved in Title IX compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance on what constitutes a Title IX "formal complaint," when institutions must investigate or otherwise respond to reports of sexual harassment, and the procedural and substantive obligations (supportive measures, grievance processes, documentation, retaliation protections) that recipients must follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal complaint definition (initiation of investigation)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'formal complaint' requires a document 'alleging sexual harassment against a respondent' that is written and signed and requests an investigation, and may be filed by the complainant or signed by the Title IX Coordinator to initiate a grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department revised §106.30 to broaden the definition of what constitutes a written, signed document, simplify filing, state that at the time of filing the complainant must be participating or attempting to participate in the recipient's education program or activity, and clarify that signing a formal complaint does not make a Title IX Coordinator a party to a grievance process. The formal complaint need not contain a detailed statement of facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient obligation to respond to actual knowledge promptly and non-deliberately indifferent
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a recipient has actual knowledge of sexual harassment in its education program or activity, it must respond promptly in a manner that is not clearly unreasonable in light of the known circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This response obligation is distinct from and broader than the obligation to investigate; it always requires offering supportive measures and taking steps appropriate to the circumstances even if no formal complaint is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer supportive measures regardless of formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer supportive measures to the complainant irrespective of whether a formal complaint is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.44(a) requires the Title IX Coordinator to contact the complainant to discuss availability of supportive measures, consider the complainant's wishes regarding such measures, and explain how to file a formal complaint. No written statement is required to receive supportive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation/grievance process triggered by formal complaint or Title IX Coordinator signature
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must investigate allegations in a formal complaint and initiate the grievance process when the complainant files, or the Title IX Coordinator signs, a formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The formal complaint requirement clarifies when the recipient's response must include investigation and adjudication versus when the recipient need only offer supportive measures and other non-investigative responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator discretion to sign a formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX Coordinator may sign a formal complaint to initiate a grievance process even if the complainant does not file one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows the recipient to investigate where a non-deliberately indifferent response requires investigation, for example to address serial perpetrators or protect the educational community, while respecting complainant autonomy to the extent possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: No statute of limitations/‘without undue delay’ requirement for filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to impose a time limit such as 'without undue delay' or other statute of limitations on a complainant's decision to file a formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposing a time limit could be unfair given trauma-related delays; the grievance process must account for any effect of passage of time on memories and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actual knowledge may be conveyed by any person and in any form
rubrics_metrics.description: Actual knowledge of sexual harassment can be conveyed to a recipient by any person—not only the complainant—and need not be in writing; anonymous reports qualify as notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must respond to information about sexual harassment from whatever source it comes, offering supportive measures and assessing whether a grievance process is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient must not impose disciplinary sanctions without following §106.45 grievance process
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are precluded from imposing disciplinary sanctions on a respondent without first following a grievance process that complies with §106.45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protects due process for respondents and ensures allegations are adjudicated under the prescribed procedures before sanctions are imposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of reasons for decisions to initiate or not initiate grievance process
rubrics_metrics.description: When a recipient decides to initiate a grievance process over a complainant's wishes, or otherwise exercises discretion, it must document its reasons showing the response was not deliberately indifferent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.45(b)(10) requires recipients to record reasons why their response to sexual harassment was not deliberately indifferent, emphasizing careful, intentional decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complainant autonomy over initiating grievance process
rubrics_metrics.description: Complainants retain control over whether their disclosure leads to a formal grievance process; reporting (oral or written) can be separate from filing a formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The formal complaint requirement is intended to ensure a grievance process results from an intentional decision by the complainant or the Title IX Coordinator, reducing retraumatization and confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third parties cannot file formal complaints (formal complaint limitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The §106.30 definition of 'formal complaint' precludes third parties (other than the Title IX Coordinator) from filing formal complaints that initiate a grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any person may report or disclose sexual harassment (which triggers response obligations), but only the complainant or the Title IX Coordinator may file/sign a formal complaint that requires investigation under §106.45.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients must inform complainants of option and process for filing formal complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must inform complainants how to file a formal complaint and that filing is optional and not required to receive supportive measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title IX Coordinators should explain the grievance process and provide clear options so complainants can make informed decisions about pursuing an investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process must afford strong due process protections to both parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The grievance process prescribed in §106.45 must provide robust due process protections for complainants and respondents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department believes §106.45's procedures appropriately safeguard fundamental fairness and reliability of Title IX proceedings for both parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient response obligations distinguish between responding and initiating investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations distinguish the recipient's duty to respond (offer supportive measures, not be deliberately indifferent) from the specific duty to initiate investigation/adjudication, which is triggered by a formal complaint or Title IX Coordinator signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarification ensures recipients do not ignore reports while also respecting complainant autonomy and conserving resources unless an investigation is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on retaliation including right not to participate
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.71 prohibits retaliation against any person exercising rights under Title IX, including the right not to participate in a grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protection guards against coercion or punishment for refusing to participate and supports complainant autonomy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to provide written notice of allegations when grievance initiated
rubrics_metrics.description: When a grievance process is initiated, recipients must prepare and send written notice of allegations to both parties (per §106.45(b)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A properly drafted formal complaint enables the recipient to prepare the written notice advising parties of essential details and important rights available under the grievance process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition alignment for elementary and secondary schools
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department adds a definition of 'elementary and secondary schools' that aligns with 'educational institutions' in 34 CFR 106.2(k): a local educational agency (LEA) as defined in ESEA, a preschool, or a private elementary or secondary school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition applies to §§106.44 and 106.45 and distinguishes K–12 entities from postsecondary institutions for the regulations' purposes.
